name: Antidisestablishmentarianism
summary: Opposition to removing the Church of England's established status, meaning its legal tie to the Crown, Parliament and state ceremony. Defenders argue, in the Church's own account, that establishment gives every parish a Christian presence and every person a right to the Church's rites, and, in Phillip Blond's, that it tempers extremism. It is a single-issue stance: the defining sources speak only to church and state.
scope: The English defence of the Church of England's establishment against disestablishment (the Liberal campaigns from the 19th century, in England, Ireland and Wales), as the dictionary, Wikipedia and the Church's own accounts of establishment state it. Richard Hooker is the classic theorist of church and commonwealth, but no defining source ties his texts to the position by name, so they answer nothing here. Excludes the positions of individual defenders on other issues and the Church of England's own teaching on them.

notes: Single-issue position.
